report: Checked all 8 candidate lemmas; none is a split. הוּא suffixes, וְ (and/But), לְ (to/for/of/unto) and הַ (the in the superscription, substantival That in v3) each take the word the ASV wrote for them in context.

אֱלֹהִים: O God in v1 and v5 is the vocative with its supplied O (rule 36); God in v4 is the jussive's subject and takes no O. אָמַר: let ... say (v4, jussive with volitive frame) vs say (v3, participle after a substantival article) is licensed by the morphology.

בָּקַשׁ: v2 That seek after (bare relative, after being the verb's supplied preposition under rule 44) and v4 those that seek (supplied antecedent plus relative under rule 46) both keep the supplied English with the anarthrous construct participle, headed on seek; the difference is what the ASV wrote, not the analysis.

חוּשׁ: v1 realizes the one clause-final imperative twice (italic Make haste at the head, Make haste again before the second infinitive) as one discontinuous unit under rules 25/34, headed on haste; v5 writes it once. Same treatment, headed on haste both times, matching the corpus (PSA.71.12, PSA.141.1).

BSB disagreements: the two paragogic he tokens on חוּשָׁה (Sh, v1 s010 and v5 s008) are unrepresented here and represented in BSB. That is the documented rule 32 convention (BSB attaches the he to its host), not an error; the tag is Sh, not the directive Sd.

The two repeated notes (paragogic he rule 32; vocative O rule 36) restate contract rules and need no convention. The superscription's Chief Musician head on Musician is a single occurrence with the competing head named in its note under rule 8; no cross-chapter precedent for נָצַח was in the packet, so it is left as accepted. Nothing generalises: no promotions or amendments.
